purpose: Teach: 版画/トランク/牡蠣/酒場/風呂敷/ヒーター/白髪/笹

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが版画作りに通われたぞ
lines.en: You know, when your father was young, he used to go make woodblock prints.
lines.style: Soft, distant gaze into memory. Measured pace. Slight lift at the end—inviting her to remember alongside him, not lecturing.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、お土産をトランクに詰めて帰られたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Oh yes, your father would pack little souvenirs into a trunk when he came home, wouldn't he?
lines.style: Warm, conversational. Gentle correction wrapped in affection—she remembers too, and wants him to know. Speaking to him as much as confirming memory.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんと牡蠣を食べに行ったぞ
lines.en: When he was young, your father and I went out to eat oysters together.
lines.style: The same distant tone as before. Quieter this time. The memory lands softer—something more intimate just below the surface.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、戦友と酒場で集まっていらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Oh, he used to gather at the tavern with his war friends, didn't he?
lines.style: Gentle affirmation. Not correcting him—meeting him halfway. A small smile in her voice. The rhythm of a very old couple speaking.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが大事な書類を風呂敷に包まれたぞ
lines.en: Back then, your father wrapped important documents so carefully in cloth.
lines.style: Quieter still. The wistfulness deepens—not sad, but tender with time passing. Breath slightly held on the memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、冬は灯油ヒーターでお部屋を暖められたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Mmm, and in winter you would warm the rooms with that kerosene heater, wouldn't you?
lines.style: Soft correction again. She's gently redirecting—not unkindly. Remembering him as the one who cared for their comfort. Voice warm and certain.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、お父さんは白髪が増えてもダンディだったぞ
lines.en: Even as your father's hair turned grey, he remained so handsome.
lines.style: The faintest smile—pride mixed with acceptance of time. Steady, not melancholy. A simple statement of fact and affection.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、七夕に笹飾りを作って下さったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: You made those beautiful bamboo decorations for Tanabata, remember? You always did that for us.
lines.style: Tender and direct. She's gently insisting on truth—he was the one who made beauty for them. Voice steady, eyes soft, a little firmer in her care.
